concepts.name: Hiragana character set
concepts.summary: Recall the 46 basic hiragana, their sounds, and their stroke order, including dakuten and handakuten variants.

concepts.name: Katakana character set
concepts.summary: Recall the katakana characters and recognise their use for loanwords, foreign names and emphasis.

concepts.name: Mora-based pronunciation rhythm
concepts.summary: Understand that Japanese is timed in morae and distinguish long vowels, geminate consonants and contracted sounds like kya.

concepts.name: Basic sentence order
concepts.summary: Explain that the verb or predicate comes at the end of the sentence and that subjects and objects are often omitted.

concepts.name: Copula desu sentences
concepts.summary: Understand how to state and identify things with X wa Y desu and form simple questions with ka.

concepts.name: Core topic and object particles
concepts.summary: Understand the basic roles of wa for topic, wo for object and no for possession.

concepts.name: Greetings and set phrases
concepts.summary: Remember everyday expressions such as konnichiwa, arigatou gozaimasu and sumimasen and when they are used.

concepts.name: Numbers and basic kanji
concepts.summary: Recall numbers up to 10,000 and a first set of simple kanji such as the digits, day, month and person.

misconceptions.text: Japanese is written with a single script where every character is a word.
The particle wa is read and written as ha in every word.
Long vowels and short vowels are interchangeable because they sound almost the same.

concepts.name: Verb groups and dictionary form
concepts.summary: Classify verbs as ichidan, godan or irregular and derive the dictionary form from the masu stem.

concepts.name: Polite verb conjugation
concepts.summary: Conjugate verbs into present, past and negative masu forms and use them in polite sentences.

concepts.name: Existence verbs aru and iru
concepts.summary: Use aru for inanimate and iru for animate existence with correct particles to describe locations.

concepts.name: Location and direction particles
concepts.summary: Choose ni, de, he and to correctly for time, place of existence, place of action, destination and companions.

concepts.name: I-adjectives and na-adjectives
concepts.summary: Conjugate both adjective types in present, past and negative and connect them to nouns.

concepts.name: Te-form basics
concepts.summary: Form the te-form for each verb group and use it for requests, sequencing and the progressive teiru.

concepts.name: Basic counters
concepts.summary: Use common counters such as tsu, nin, mai and hon with numbers and the correct sound changes.

concepts.name: Kanji readings introduction
concepts.summary: Distinguish on'yomi from kun'yomi readings and read common N5 kanji in simple compounds.

misconceptions.text: Wa and ga are interchangeable and mean the same thing.
Every verb ending in -eru or -iru is an ichidan verb.
Counters can be replaced by the plain number and a noun as in English.

concepts.name: Wa versus ga contrast
concepts.summary: Analyse when wa marks a known or contrasted topic and ga marks new information or the focus of the sentence.

concepts.name: Plain form and casual speech
concepts.summary: Use plain forms of verbs and adjectives in casual speech and in embedded clauses.

concepts.name: Nai-form and ta-form patterns
concepts.summary: Apply the nai and ta forms in patterns such as nakereba naranai and tara conditionals.

concepts.name: Conditional forms comparison
concepts.summary: Distinguish to, ba, tara and nara conditionals by nuance, and choose the appropriate one.

concepts.name: Relative clauses
concepts.summary: Analyse and build clauses that modify nouns using plain forms, with ga replacing wa inside the clause.

concepts.name: Potential and passive forms
concepts.summary: Form and use potential, passive and causative forms of each verb group, noting object particle changes.

concepts.name: Giving and receiving verbs
concepts.summary: Analyse the direction of benefit expressed by ageru, kureru and morau and their te-form uses.

concepts.name: Kanji compound reading strategies
concepts.summary: Infer readings of kanji compounds from on'yomi and kun'yomi patterns and recognise common exceptions.

misconceptions.text: Ga marks the subject and wa marks the subject too, so the choice is only a matter of style.
Tara, ba, to and nara conditionals can always be swapped without a change in meaning.
The passive form is used only when the subject is harmed, as in English passive voice.

concepts.name: Keigo system structure
concepts.summary: Analyse the three keigo categories of respectful, humble and polite speech and who each raises or lowers.

concepts.name: Uchi-soto social perspective
concepts.summary: Evaluate how in-group and out-group relations decide the keigo level, including speaking about one's own family to outsiders.

concepts.name: Honorific and humble verb forms
concepts.summary: Choose between special verbs like irassharu and mairu and productive patterns like o-V ni naru and o-V suru for a given context.

concepts.name: Formal written grammar patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse N3 to N2 patterns such as wake, hazu, ni tsuite and ni yotte and distinguish their nuance.

concepts.name: Modality and evidential expressions
concepts.summary: Evaluate the evidential strength of souda, rashii, you da and mitai to select the most accurate expression.

concepts.name: Kanji vocabulary at N2 level
concepts.summary: Analyse the structure of abstract compounds and use radicals and components to deduce meaning of unfamiliar kanji.

concepts.name: Causative-passive and nuance verbs
concepts.summary: Analyse the causative-passive and aspectual auxiliaries like te shimau and te oku for implied attitude.

misconceptions.text: Keigo means adding more polite words, so using the honorific form for oneself is the most respectful choice.
Masu form alone is enough for every formal or business situation.
Souda, rashii, you da and mitai are all synonyms for it seems.

concepts.name: Register and style shifting
concepts.summary: Evaluate and manage shifts between plain, polite, honorific and written registers to fit the relationship, medium and intent.

concepts.name: Pragmatics of indirectness
concepts.summary: Evaluate how hedging, omission and sentence-final particles convey stance and avoid direct refusal.

concepts.name: Authentic text analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate dense news, essays and literature by resolving implied subjects, nominalisations and long modification chains.

concepts.name: Literary and classical grammar remnants
concepts.summary: Evaluate how forms like nari, beki and zu survive in modern writing, proverbs and formal documents.

concepts.name: Idiomatic and mimetic expression
concepts.summary: Create natural expression using onomatopoeia, idioms and four-character compounds appropriate to context.

concepts.name: Composing formal and business writing
concepts.summary: Compose emails, reports and persuasive essays with correct keigo, conventional openings and cohesive structure.

concepts.name: Dialect and variation awareness
concepts.summary: Evaluate regional dialects, gendered and generational speech and decide when to understand versus produce them.

misconceptions.text: Mastering JLPT N1 vocabulary and patterns means a learner can write and speak naturally in every context.
Textbook Japanese is the standard form that every native speaker uses in daily conversation.
Ambiguity and omission in Japanese are signs of vague thinking and should be replaced with explicit subjects in all writing.
